# FlowGuard — Google Cloud Run deployment (asia-southeast1)

Project: `flowguard-502613`
Artifact Registry: `asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers`

Three services, deployed in this order (each later service needs the earlier one's URL):

| Service            | Source        | Image name          | What it runs                          |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `flowguard-server` | `server/`     | `flowguard-server`  | Node.js/Express API (`node index.js`) |
| `flowguard-ai`     | `ai-service/` | `flowguard-ai`      | FastAPI + InsightFace + YOLOv8 (uvicorn) |
| `flowguard-client` | `client/`     | `flowguard-client`  | React static build behind Nginx reverse proxy |

## Architecture

Same-origin reverse proxy — the browser only ever talks to the frontend origin:

```
Browser ──► flowguard-client (Nginx)
              ├── /api/*, /user/*  ──► flowguard-server (Node)
              ├── /ai/*  (prefix stripped) ──► flowguard-ai (FastAPI YOLO endpoints)
              └── everything else ──► React SPA (index.html fallback for React Router)

flowguard-server ──► flowguard-ai   (face endpoints, X-AI-Service-Key)
flowguard-ai     ──► flowguard-server (detection alerts, x-service-key)
Both            ──► PostgreSQL (external: Neon/Supabase/Cloud SQL)
```

Why this architecture (instead of a build-time `VITE_API_BASE_URL`):

- The Object Detection pages call `/ai/api/yolo/*` as **hardcoded relative
  paths** that previously only worked through the Vite dev proxy. The Nginx
  proxy reproduces that mapping in production with **zero frontend code changes**.
- No backend URL, key, or secret is baked into the image or JS bundle; the
  backend hosts are injected at container start (`BACKEND_HOST`, `AI_HOST`).
- No CORS surface: the browser sees a single origin. Backend CORS
  (`CLIENT_URL`) and AI CORS (`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) remain as defence in depth.
- `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is deliberately left **empty** at build time.

## Cloud Run compliance checklist (already handled in code/images)

- **PORT**: Node resolves `PORT → APP_PORT → 5001` (`server/config/serverConfig.js`);
  the AI image starts `uvicorn --port ${PORT:-8080}`; Nginx listens on `${PORT}`
  via the official image's envsubst templates. **Never set PORT manually** on a
  Cloud Run service — it is injected.
- **0.0.0.0** binding on all three services.
- **No nodemon in production** — the server image installs `--omit=dev` and runs
  `node index.js` (also available as `npm start`).
- **SPA fallback** — Nginx `try_files ... /index.html` for React Router deep links.
- **No localhost between services** — `FACE_AI_URL`, `NODE_SERVER_URL`,
  `PYTHON_AI_URL`, `BACKEND_HOST`, `AI_HOST` all come from env vars.
- **Models baked at build time** — buffalo_l (InsightFace) and yolov8n.pt are
  inside the AI image; nothing downloads at cold start or per request.

## Build & push (run from the repo root — DO NOT run until you intend to deploy)

```bash
gcloud auth configure-docker asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev

REG=asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers

docker build -t $REG/flowguard-server:v1 server/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 ai-service/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-client:v1 \
  --build-arg VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=<public-site-key> client/

docker push $REG/flowguard-server:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-ai:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-client:v1
```

(Or `gcloud builds submit` per directory with the same tags.)

## Deploy

Put every secret in **Secret Manager** first (`APP_SECRET`, `DB_PWD`,
`AI_SERVICE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `SMTP_PASS`, `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN`, …)
and grant the runtime service account `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`.
See [env.example](env.example) for the full variable list per service.

```bash
REGION=asia-southeast1

# 1) Backend
gcloud run deploy flowguard-server \
  --image $REG/flowguard-server:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 1Gi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,DB_SYNC_ALTER=false \
  --set-secrets APP_SECRET=APP_SECRET:latest,DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest,RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:latest,SMTP_PASS=SMTP_PASS:latest,EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN=EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN:latest
# note the URL it prints -> SERVER_URL

# 2) AI service (URL of the backend now exists)
gcloud run deploy flowguard-ai \
  --image $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 4Gi --cpu 2 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 \
  --concurrency 8 --timeout 300 --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,NODE_SERVER_URL=$SERVER_URL,USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false,FACE_CTX_ID=-1 \
  --set-secrets DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest
# note the URL -> AI_URL

# 3) Frontend (hostnames only, no https://)
gcloud run deploy flowguard-client \
  --image $REG/flowguard-client:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 512Mi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars BACKEND_HOST=${SERVER_URL#https://},AI_HOST=${AI_URL#https://}
# note the URL -> CLIENT_URL

# 4) Point the backend's CORS + links at the real frontend URL
gcloud run services update flowguard-server --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars CLIENT_URL=$CLIENT_URL,FRONTEND_URL=$CLIENT_URL

# 5) Tell the AI service which browser origin is allowed (defence in depth)
gcloud run services update flowguard-ai --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars ALLOWED_ORIGINS=$CLIENT_URL
```

## Recommended resources

| Service            | Memory | CPU | Concurrency | Notes |
|--------------------|--------|-----|-------------|-------|
| `flowguard-client` | 512 Mi | 1   | default (80)| Nginx + static files; 256 Mi also works |
| `flowguard-server` | 1 Gi   | 1   | default (80)| Sequelize sync on boot; 50 MB JSON bodies |
| `flowguard-ai`     | **4 Gi** | **2** | **8**   | buffalo_l (det+recog ONNX) + YOLOv8n resident ≈ 1.5–2.5 GB RSS; per-request numpy/cv2 spikes. 2 vCPU keeps analyze-frame latency usable on CPU. Set `--timeout 300`. |

AI image size estimate: **≈ 2.5–3.5 GB** (CPU torch ≈ 900 MB, torchvision,
2× OpenCV wheels, onnxruntime, buffalo_l pack ≈ 280 MB, yolov8n.pt 6.5 MB).
Consider `--min-instances 1` for the AI service if cold starts (model load
≈ 10–30 s) are unacceptable for the demo.

## PDPA & security controls

- **Biometric data never enters an image**: `.dockerignore` files exclude
  `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, screenshots, recordings, databases,
  logs, model caches, `node_modules`, `.venv`, tests, and `.git`.
- **Secrets** live in Secret Manager only — never in Dockerfiles, build args,
  or `VITE_` variables (every `VITE_` value ships to the browser).
- **Face endpoints** (`/api/encode-faces`, `/user/recognize`, `/user/track`,
  `/refresh`) require `AI_SERVICE_KEY` — set it on BOTH services or the AI
  service runs unprotected (it prints a warning in dev mode).
- The AI service returns **user IDs, not names**, to callers; names appear in
  developer logs only. Embeddings stay in PostgreSQL; the recognize path never
  persists frames.
- **PDPA retention**: the backend's 90-day transcript cleanup cron starts with
  the server process.
- **Raspberry Pi**: no private Pi IP is baked into the public bundle (the
  fallback is the mDNS name `raspberrypi.local`; real Pi URLs come from
  `VITE_PI_CAMERA_*` env at build for kiosk builds only). The SecurePi edge
  node pushes alerts *outbound* to `/api/edge/detection-alerts` with
  `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN` — the cloud never needs to reach into the LAN.
- Nginx adds `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a referrer
  policy; body size is capped at 50 MB to match the backend.

## Local smoke test

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 --env-file server/.env  <server-image>
docker run --rm -p 8081:8081 -e PORT=8081 --env-file ai-service/.env <ai-image>
docker run --rm -p 8082:8082 -e PORT=8082 \
  -e BACKEND_HOST=<server-host> -e AI_HOST=<ai-host> <client-image>
```

```bash
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars BACKEND_HOST=${SERVER_URL#https://},AI_HOST=${AI_URL#https://}
# note the URL -> CLIENT_URL

# 4) Point the backend's CORS + links at the real frontend URL
gcloud run services update flowguard-server --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars CLIENT_URL=$CLIENT_URL,FRONTEND_URL=$CLIENT_URL

# 5) Tell the AI service which browser origin is allowed (defence in depth)
gcloud run services update flowguard-ai --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars ALLOWED_ORIGINS=$CLIENT_URL
```

## Recommended resources

| Service            | Memory | CPU | Concurrency | Notes |
|--------------------|--------|-----|-------------|-------|
| `flowguard-client` | 512 Mi | 1   | default (80)| Nginx + static files; 256 Mi also works |
| `flowguard-server` | 1 Gi   | 1   | default (80)| Sequelize sync on boot; 50 MB JSON bodies |
| `flowguard-ai`     | **4 Gi** | **2** | **8**   | buffalo_l (det+recog ONNX) + YOLOv8n resident ≈ 1.5–2.5 GB RSS; per-request numpy/cv2 spikes. 2 vCPU keeps analyze-frame latency usable on CPU. Set `--timeout 300`. |

AI image size estimate: **≈ 2.5–3.5 GB** (CPU torch ≈ 900 MB, torchvision,
2× OpenCV wheels, onnxruntime, buffalo_l pack ≈ 280 MB, yolov8n.pt 6.5 MB).
Consider `--min-instances 1` for the AI service if cold starts (model load
≈ 10–30 s) are unacceptable for the demo.

## PDPA & security controls

- **Biometric data never enters an image**: `.dockerignore` files exclude
  `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, screenshots, recordings, databases,
  logs, model caches, `node_modules`, `.venv`, tests, and `.git`.
- **Secrets** live in Secret Manager only — never in Dockerfiles, build args,
  or `VITE_` variables (every `VITE_` value ships to the browser).
- **Face endpoints** (`/api/encode-faces`, `/user/recognize`, `/user/track`,
  `/refresh`) require `AI_SERVICE_KEY` — set it on BOTH services or the AI
  service runs unprotected (it prints a warning in dev mode).
- The AI service returns **user IDs, not names**, to callers; names appear in
  developer logs only. Embeddings stay in PostgreSQL; the recognize path never
  persists frames.
- **PDPA retention**: the backend's 90-day transcript cleanup cron starts with
  the server process.
- **Raspberry Pi**: no private Pi IP is baked into the public bundle (the
  fallback is the mDNS name `raspberrypi.local`; real Pi URLs come from
  `VITE_PI_CAMERA_*` env at build for kiosk builds only). The SecurePi edge
  node pushes alerts *outbound* to `/api/edge/detection-alerts` with
  `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN` — the cloud never needs to reach into the LAN.
- Nginx adds `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a referrer
  policy; body size is capped at 50 MB to match the backend.

## Local smoke test

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 --env-file server/.env  <server-image>
docker run --rm -p 8081:8081 -e PORT=8081 --env-file ai-service/.env <ai-image>
docker run --rm -p 8082:8082 -e PORT=8082 \
  -e BACKEND_HOST=<server-host> -e AI_HOST=<ai-host> <client-image>
```

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# FlowGuard Python AI service (FastAPI + InsightFace + YOLOv8) — Cloud Run image.
#
# Key decisions:
#   - CPU-only PyTorch wheels (download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu): Cloud Run has no
#     GPU here, and the default PyPI torch wheel bundles CUDA (~2+ GB saved).
#     main.py already runs everything on CPU (FACE_CTX_ID=-1 default,
#     onnxruntime CPU provider), so CPU execution support is preserved.
#   - insightface==0.7.3 has no prebuilt Linux wheel — it compiles C++/Cython,
#     hence the build-essential builder stage. The runtime stage ships no
#     compiler toolchain.
#   - Models are baked in at BUILD time, never downloaded per request or per
#     cold start:
#       * yolov8n.pt is copied from the repo (standard COCO weights — contains
#         no personal data);
#       * the InsightFace "buffalo_l" model pack is downloaded once during the
#         build into the app user's ~/.insightface cache.
#   - Listens on the Cloud Run-injected PORT, binds 0.0.0.0, started by
#     uvicorn (the __main__ block's hardcoded 8501 is dev-only and unused here).
#   - USE_SERVER_CAMERA stays false: no physical webcam exists on Cloud Run;
#     frames arrive from the browser via /api/yolo/analyze-frame.
#   - No secrets baked in — DB_*, AI_SERVICE_KEY, NODE_SERVER_URL etc. come
#     from Cloud Run env vars / Secret Manager. .env excluded by .dockerignore.

FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential g++ \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
WORKDIR /build
COPY requirements.txt .
# CPU torch first (satisfies the torch==2.11.0 / torchvision==0.26.0 pins),
# then the rest of the pinned requirements.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir torch==2.11.0 torchvision==0.26.0 \
        --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu \
    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

FROM python:3.12-slim
# OpenCV (cv2) runtime libraries only — no compilers in the final image.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        libgl1 libglib2.0-0 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1001 appuser
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    # Writable config/cache dirs for ultralytics + matplotlib on a read-only-ish FS.
    YOLO_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/ultralytics \
    MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/matplotlib \
    USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

USER appuser
WORKDIR /app

# Bake the InsightFace buffalo_l pack into the image at build time so cold
# starts never download models. (~280 MB into /home/appuser/.insightface)
RUN python -c "from insightface.app import FaceAnalysis; FaceAnalysis(name='buffalo_l', providers=['CPUExecutionProvider'])"

# Copy only the application files — never .env, .venv, tests, or face images.
COPY --chown=appuser:appuser main.py zone_rules.py yolo_service.py yolov8n.pt ./

# Documentation only — Cloud Run supplies PORT and routes to it.
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["sh", "-c", "exec uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080}"]

content.text:
All done — every deliverable is in place, all validation passed, and everything is left unstaged.

## 1. Files created or changed

**Created:** [server/Dockerfile](server/Dockerfile), [server/.dockerignore](server/.dockerignore), [client/Dockerfile](client/Dockerfile), [client/.dockerignore](client/.dockerignore), [client/nginx.conf](client/nginx.conf) (Nginx **is** used — it's an envsubst template), [ai-service/Dockerfile](ai-service/Dockerfile), [ai-service/.dockerignore](ai-service/.dockerignore), [deployment/cloud-run/README.md](deployment/cloud-run/README.md), [deployment/cloud-run/env.example](deployment/cloud-run/env.example).

**Modified (2 minimal code changes):**
- [server/package.json](server/package.json) — added `"start": "node index.js"` (production start without nodemon).
- [piCamera.js:6](client/src/constants/piCamera.js:6) — the fallback Pi camera URL was the private IP `172.20.10.4` baked into the public JS bundle; replaced with the mDNS name `raspberrypi.local`. Verified the rebuilt bundle contains no private IPs or localhost URLs.

## 2. Recommended architecture & Cloud Run compatibility

**Same-origin reverse proxy (recommended and implemented).** The Object Detection pages call `/ai/api/yolo/*` as hardcoded relative paths that only worked through the Vite dev proxy — a build-time `VITE_API_BASE_URL` would not fix those. The Nginx container reproduces the dev-proxy mapping (`/api`+`/user` → Node, `/ai` → FastAPI with prefix stripped) with zero frontend code changes, no CORS surface, and no backend URL baked into the image. Backend hostnames are injected at container start (`BACKEND_HOST`, `AI_HOST`) via Nginx's template mechanism. `VITE_API_BASE_URL` stays empty on purpose.

Compliance: Node already resolved `PORT → APP_PORT → 5001` on `0.0.0.0` ([serverConfig.js](server/config/serverConfig.js)); the AI image starts `uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080}` (main.py's hardcoded 8501 is only in the dev-only `__main__` block); Nginx listens on `${PORT}`; SPA deep links fall back to `index.html`; no service sets PORT itself.

## 3. Environment variables (exact names, full list in [env.example](deployment/cloud-run/env.example))

- **flowguard-server**: secrets `APP_SECRET, DB_PWD, AI_SERVICE_KEY, RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY, SMTP_PASS, EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN, EDGE_SERVICE_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`; plain `CLIENT_URL, ALLOWED_ORIGINS, FRONTEND_URL, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, FACE_AI_URL, PYTHON_AI_URL, DB_SYNC_ALTER, SMTP_HOST/PORT/SECURE/USER, MAIL_FROM, WHATSAPP_*`
- **flowguard-ai**: secrets `DB_PWD, AI_SERVICE_KEY` (must match the server's); plain `DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, NODE_SERVER_URL, ALLOWED_ORIGINS, USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false, FACE_CTX_ID=-1, AI_CAMERA_LOCATION`
- **flowguard-client**: runtime `BACKEND_HOST, AI_HOST` (hostnames only); build-arg `VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public value — the only build arg, and BuildKit's linter flags it purely on the `_KEY` name heuristic)

## 4. Build blockers

**None.** All three images built end-to-end locally. Notes: `insightface==0.7.3` compiles from source (handled by the build-essential builder stage), and torch is installed from the CPU wheel index to avoid ~2 GB of CUDA payload.

## 5. Recommended resources

| Service | Memory | CPU | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| flowguard-client | 512 Mi | 1 | Nginx + static; image 142 MB |
| flowguard-server | 1 Gi | 1 | 50 MB JSON bodies, Sequelize sync on boot; image 375 MB |
| flowguard-ai | **4 Gi** | **2** | concurrency 8, timeout 300 s; image **4.37 GB**; consider `--min-instances 1` (model load ≈ 10–30 s on cold start) |

## 6. PDPA & security controls

`.dockerignore` files exclude `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, recordings, databases, logs, model caches, tests, and `.git` — I verified the built server image contains no `.env` or tests. Secrets go to Secret Manager only, never Dockerfiles or `VITE_` values. `AI_SERVICE_KEY` must be set on both services or the face endpoints run unprotected (main.py warns). The AI service returns user IDs, not names; frames are never persisted; the 90-day transcript cleanup cron runs with the server. No Pi private IP ships in the bundle; SecurePi pushes outbound with `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN`. CPU execution preserved (`FACE_CTX_ID=-1`, onnxruntime CPU provider, CPU torch).

## 7. Test results — all passing

- Client Vitest: **433/433** (47 files) · Client `npm run build`: **OK**
- Server Jest: **389/389** (28 suites)
- Python pytest (`ai-service/tests`): **8/8**
- `docker build --check`: clean for all three (only the site-key naming heuristic warning)
- Real builds + smoke tests: client container serves the SPA with deep-link fallback on an injected PORT; AI container loads YOLO + buffalo_l **from the baked-in cache with no runtime download** and answers `/api/yolo/people-count`

## 8. Git state

Nothing committed, pushed, or staged — `git status` shows only unstaged modifications and untracked new files; HEAD remains at `f28a005` on `deploy/staging`. No cloud resources were touched. (I did start Docker Desktop locally to run the build validation.)

content:
Review the completed FlowGuard Cloud Run preparation before I commit it.

The current implementation uses the public client Nginx container to proxy both:

- /api to the Node service
- /ai to the Python AI service

For a real-world PDPA-sensitive deployment, the Python AI Cloud Run service must
not be anonymously accessible.

Change the deployment architecture to:

Browser/client → Node backend → private Python AI service

Requirements:

1. The client Nginx service may proxy /api only to the Node backend.

2. Remove direct client/Nginx proxying of /ai to the Python service.

3. Update Object Detection frontend requests currently using:
   /ai/api/yolo/people-count
   /ai/api/yolo/analyze-frame

   so they call equivalent Node endpoints.

4. Add or reuse secure Node proxy routes for:
   - people count
   - frame analysis
   - facial tracking
   - facial recognition

5. Node must call the Python AI service using FACE_AI_URL/PYTHON_AI_URL.

6. Prepare Node for private Cloud Run service-to-service authentication:
   - obtain a Google-signed ID token for the AI service audience using Google
     application default credentials / the Cloud Run service account;
   - send it using Authorization or X-Serverless-Authorization;
   - preserve X-AI-Service-Key as defence in depth;
   - keep local development working without requiring Google credentials.

7. Do not put service-account JSON key files in the repository or container.
   Cloud Run must use its attached service account identity.

8. The AI service should be deployed without allowing unauthenticated access.
   Document that the Node service account requires roles/run.invoker on the AI
   service.

9. Remove raspberrypi.local as an automatic cloud fallback.
   The cloud build should have no default Pi address.
   Preserve browser camera, uploaded video and authenticated edge-ingestion
   fallbacks.

10. Keep:
   - React Router fallback;
   - Cloud Run PORT handling;
   - existing RBAC;
   - AI_SERVICE_KEY validation;
   - CPU InsightFace/YOLO support;
   - all current functionality.

11. Update:
   - client/nginx.conf
   - deployment/cloud-run/README.md
   - deployment/cloud-run/env.example
   - deployment commands
   - relevant Node and client source/tests

12. Validate:
   - client full tests
   - client production build
   - server full tests
   - Python tests
   - all three Docker builds
   - container smoke tests

Do not deploy, commit, push, stage, reset or create cloud resources.

Return:
1. architecture change made;
2. routes changed;
3. private AI authentication implementation;
4. local-development fallback;
5. Pi URL behaviour;
6. files changed;
7. all test/build results;
8. confirmation nothing committed or pushed.

I need to set up Node proxy routes for the YOLO endpoints that the client is calling—specifically the people-count and frame analysis endpoints. I'll create a new route file to handle these requests while keeping the existing ObjectDetection and CameraFeed components intact.

The key thing is figuring out the authentication pattern. The facial recognition routes already exist and go through Node via a proxy to FACE_AI_URL, so I should follow that same pattern for YOLO. I need to check how the client is currently authenticating these requests—whether it's passing an Authorization header—and then apply the same middleware (validateToken) to the new YOLO routes to maintain the existing RBAC for authenticated FM users.

For the Google ID token, I'm leaning toward using the Cloud Run metadata server directly via a simple HTTP request rather than adding a new dependency. On Cloud Run, I can hit the metadata endpoint to get an identity token for the AI service audience, and for local development I'll just skip it since the metadata server won't be available. This keeps things lightweight and aligns with how Cloud Run's service account identity works.

On the authorization header front, I can send the ID token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` without conflicts since the FastAPI service doesn't validate Authorization itself—the Cloud Run IAM layer handles that before the app sees it. I'll keep the existing `X-AI-Service-Key` header alongside it.

Now I need to find where the Node-to-AI calls are happening, starting with facialRecognition.js. Updating the client-side URLs in ObjectDetection and CameraFeed components to point to the new `/api/yolo/` endpoints instead of `/ai/api/yolo/`, and making sure the test files reflect those changes. I also need to check for any MJPEG stream references and remove the `/ai` block from nginx, then handle the piCamera.js default by clearing it and adding guards for the reachability checks.

For the Pi camera tests, the regex assertion in PiCamera.test.jsx will fail with an empty URL string, so I need to update that test logic. Similarly, GateScannerCamera.test.jsx sets the preview src to the PI_CAMERA_STREAM_URL constant, which will be empty — the test will still pass since both sides match, but the actual page behavior should fall back to webcam when isPiCameraReachable returns false.

The trickier issue is with tests that mock a successful Pi connection: if I make isPiCameraReachable return false whenever the URL is empty, those tests will break because they're expecting the Pi mode to activate based on fetch mocks, but now reachability is hardcoded false regardless of what the fetch stub returns. I need to figure out how the tests are setting the environment variable for PI_CAMERA_STREAM_URL in the first place.

A cleaner approach: gate the fallback URL on the environment mode itself. In development and test mode, provide the default Pi address so tests work unchanged. In production, when the env var isn't set, there's no fallback — the URL stays empty and reachability fails immediately, triggering the webcam fallback. This satisfies the requirement that the cloud build has no default Pi address while keeping local development and tests working out of the box.

Now I need to set up the Node proxy route for the video stream. Now I'm considering whether the Node server should also send the service key header to the AI endpoints—it won't hurt since they ignore it anyway, so I'll include it through a shared helper. content.thinking:
CameraFeed needs to authenticate requests since it's used on a protected page, so I'll add token-based auth headers to the client calls and secure the Node YOLO proxy endpoint with role verification. I need to check the auth middleware signatures first, then update the AI service accordingly.

Now I'm setting up the server-side auth headers using Google's metadata server for ID tokens in production environments, with fallback logic to handle local development where metadata isn't available — caching failures to avoid repeated timeout delays.

The approach checks for Cloud Run indicators like the K_SERVICE environment variable or an explicit opt-in flag to decide whether to attempt token fetching, keeping local development simple and credential-free. For the audience, I'm extracting just the origin from the service URLs using the URL API, then caching tokens per audience with JWT expiry tracking to refresh about a minute before they expire. Finally, I'm sending the token as a standard Authorization Bearer header since the AI service validates through Cloud Run's IAM layer.

Now I'm setting up the YOLO routes that handle people counting and frame analysis, with middleware to verify tokens and check user roles before forwarding requests to the AI service with proper authentication headers.

Finishing the analyze-frame endpoint with a 20-second timeout, error handling that passes through 400 responses from the AI service while treating other failures as 502 errors, and whitelisting the specific body fields to forward since the AI model's Pydantic schema ignores extra fields by default.

I need to mount this route in the main index.js file, then update all the existing AI service calls across facialRecognition.js, user.js, and incident.js to use the new authentication header helper instead of the hardcoded service key approach. There are several axios calls scattered throughout those files that need this swap, and I should locate each one precisely before making changes.

On the client side, I'm updating ObjectDetection.jsx to point to the new `/api/yolo/` endpoints and include authorization headers in both the people count fetch and the frame analysis call. CameraFeed.jsx also needs the URL and header updates, pulling the token from localStorage. Then I need to check the test files — CameraFeed.test.jsx is expecting the old `/ai/api/yolo/analyze-frame` path, so that assertion needs updating, and I should verify ObjectDetectionSourceModes.test.jsx doesn't have any hardcoded `/ai/` references that would break.

For piCamera.js, I'm setting up a development fallback that uses `import.meta.env.DEV` to conditionally point to the local Raspberry Pi stream URL, but I need to verify whether vitest actually sets that DEV flag to true during test runs.

Looking at how vitest handles this: it does set `import.meta.env.DEV = true` by default in test mode unless NODE_ENV is explicitly set to production. So in tests, the fallback URL will be present and the guards like `isPiCameraReachable` will work correctly, but in production builds where DEV is false, the expression evaluates to an empty string, which the guards then catch and return false. The PiCamera tests should pass because they'll see the URLs populated during test execution.

Now I need to remove the `/ai` block from nginx.conf.

For the client Dockerfile, no changes are needed since it just copies the updated nginx.conf. But I do need to update the README and env.example: remove AI_HOST from the client service documentation, add the gcloud command to grant the invoker role to the node service account, mention that a dedicated service account is recommended, and clean up the env.example to remove AI_HOST references and note that ALLOWED_ORIGINS can be left empty since the AI service no longer handles browser traffic.

The VITE configuration doesn't need any changes. For the server environment, I should add optional audience configuration—the default audience will be derived from the origin of FACE_AI_URL and PYTHON_AI_URL separately, but I can provide optional override environment variables like FACE_AI_AUDIENCE to keep things simple and well-documented.

Now I need to look at the actual middleware and auth implementation in auth.js to see where these tokens are being validated, then check the call sites in user.js and incident.js.

# FlowGuard — Google Cloud Run deployment (asia-southeast1)

Project: `flowguard-502613`
Artifact Registry: `asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers`

Three services, deployed in this order (each later service needs the earlier one's URL):

| Service            | Source        | Image name          | Access | What it runs                          |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------------|--------|----------------------------------------|
| `flowguard-server` | `server/`     | `flowguard-server`  | public | Node.js/Express API (`node index.js`) |
| `flowguard-ai`     | `ai-service/` | `flowguard-ai`      | **PRIVATE** | FastAPI + InsightFace + YOLOv8 (uvicorn) |
| `flowguard-client` | `client/`     | `flowguard-client`  | public | React static build behind Nginx reverse proxy |

## Architecture

The AI service is **private** — it holds the biometric matching engine, so it
must never be anonymously reachable. Only the Node backend can invoke it:

```
Browser ──► flowguard-client (Nginx, public)
              ├── /api/*, /user/*  ──► flowguard-server (Node, public)
              └── everything else ──► React SPA (index.html fallback for React Router)

flowguard-server (JWT/RBAC first) ──► flowguard-ai (PRIVATE)
    /api/facial-recognition/*  -> /user/recognize, /user/track      (face)
    /user/enroll-face          -> /api/encode-faces, /refresh       (enrolment)
    /api/yolo/*                -> /api/yolo/*                       (object detection)
    each call carries: Authorization: Bearer <Google ID token>      (Cloud Run IAM)
                       X-AI-Service-Key: <shared secret>            (defence in depth)

flowguard-ai ──► flowguard-server (detection alerts, x-service-key)
Both         ──► PostgreSQL (external: Neon/Supabase/Cloud SQL)
SecurePi (LAN) ──► flowguard-server /api/edge/detection-alerts (Bearer EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN)
```

Why this architecture:

- **The AI service is deployed with `--no-allow-unauthenticated`.** Cloud Run's
  IAM layer rejects any caller without a Google-signed ID token for the AI
  service's audience — the biometric endpoints are unreachable from the
  internet even if the app-level `AI_SERVICE_KEY` ever leaked.
- The browser **never** talks to FastAPI: the old `/ai/*` passthrough is gone.
  YOLO object detection now flows through the Node proxy `/api/yolo/*`
  (JWT + FM/Staff role), like facial recognition always did.
- The Node backend obtains its ID token from the **Cloud Run metadata server**
  using the service's attached service account
  (`server/services/aiServiceAuth.js`). **No service-account JSON key file
  exists in the repo, images, or env** — Cloud Run's own identity is used.
- No backend URL or secret is baked into the client image or JS bundle; the
  backend host is injected at container start (`BACKEND_HOST`).
- `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is deliberately left **empty** at build time (relative
  URLs, same-origin Nginx proxy, no CORS surface).

## Cloud Run compliance checklist (already handled in code/images)

- **PORT**: Node resolves `PORT → APP_PORT → 5001` (`server/config/serverConfig.js`);
  the AI image starts `uvicorn --port ${PORT:-8080}`; Nginx listens on `${PORT}`
  via the official image's envsubst templates. **Never set PORT manually** on a
  Cloud Run service — it is injected.
- **0.0.0.0** binding on all three services.
- **No nodemon in production** — the server image installs `--omit=dev` and runs
  `node index.js` (also available as `npm start`).
- **SPA fallback** — Nginx `try_files ... /index.html` for React Router deep links.
- **No localhost between services** — `FACE_AI_URL`, `NODE_SERVER_URL`,
  `PYTHON_AI_URL`, `BACKEND_HOST` all come from env vars.
- **Models baked at build time** — buffalo_l (InsightFace) and yolov8n.pt are
  inside the AI image; nothing downloads at cold start or per request.
- **Private-service auth** — ID tokens are fetched from the metadata server and
  cached until shortly before expiry; locally (no `K_SERVICE`) no token is
  attempted, so `npm run dev` needs no Google credentials.

## Build & push (run from the repo root — DO NOT run until you intend to deploy)

```bash
gcloud auth configure-docker asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev

REG=asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers

docker build -t $REG/flowguard-server:v1 server/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 ai-service/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-client:v1 \
  --build-arg VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=<public-site-key> client/

docker push $REG/flowguard-server:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-ai:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-client:v1
```

(Or `gcloud builds submit` per directory with the same tags.)

## Deploy

Put every secret in **Secret Manager** first (`APP_SECRET`, `DB_PWD`,
`AI_SERVICE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `SMTP_PASS`, `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN`, …)
and grant the runtime service account `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`.
See [env.example](env.example) for the full variable list per service.

```bash
REGION=asia-southeast1

# 0) Dedicated identity for the Node backend (recommended over the default SA)
gcloud iam service-accounts create flowguard-server-sa \
  --display-name "FlowGuard Node backend"
SERVER_SA=flowguard-server-sa@flowguard-502613.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 1) Backend
gcloud run deploy flowguard-server \
  --image $REG/flowguard-server:v1 --region $REGION \
  --service-account $SERVER_SA \
  --memory 1Gi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,DB_SYNC_ALTER=false \
  --set-secrets APP_SECRET=APP_SECRET:latest,DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest,RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:latest,SMTP_PASS=SMTP_PASS:latest,EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN=EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN:latest
# note the URL it prints -> SERVER_URL

# 2) AI service — PRIVATE: no unauthenticated access, ingress restricted.
gcloud run deploy flowguard-ai \
  --image $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 4Gi --cpu 2 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 \
  --concurrency 8 --timeout 300 \
  --no-allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,NODE_SERVER_URL=$SERVER_URL,USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false,FACE_CTX_ID=-1 \
  --set-secrets DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest
# note the URL -> AI_URL

# 2b) REQUIRED: only the Node backend's service account may invoke the AI service.
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding flowguard-ai --region $REGION \
  --member serviceAccount:$SERVER_SA \
  --role roles/run.invoker

# 2c) Point the backend at the AI service (audience for its ID tokens = this URL).
gcloud run services update flowguard-server --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars FACE_AI_URL=$AI_URL

# 3) Frontend (hostname only, no https://). No AI_HOST — the AI service is private.
gcloud run deploy flowguard-client \
  --image $REG/flowguard-client:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 512Mi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars BACKEND_HOST=${SERVER_URL#https://}
# note the URL -> CLIENT_URL

# 4) Point the backend's CORS + links at the real frontend URL
gcloud run services update flowguard-server --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars CLIENT_URL=$CLIENT_URL,FRONTEND_URL=$CLIENT_URL
```

## Recommended resources

| Service            | Memory | CPU | Concurrency | Notes |
|--------------------|--------|-----|-------------|-------|
| `flowguard-client` | 512 Mi | 1   | default (80)| Nginx + static files; 256 Mi also works |
| `flowguard-server` | 1 Gi   | 1   | default (80)| Sequelize sync on boot; 50 MB JSON bodies; now also relays YOLO frames |
| `flowguard-ai`     | **4 Gi** | **2** | **8**   | buffalo_l (det+recog ONNX) + YOLOv8n resident ≈ 1.5–2.5 GB RSS; per-request numpy/cv2 spikes. 2 vCPU keeps analyze-frame latency usable on CPU. `--timeout 300`. |

AI image size ≈ **4.4 GB** (CPU torch, torchvision, 2× OpenCV wheels,
onnxruntime, buffalo_l pack ≈ 280 MB, yolov8n.pt 6.5 MB). Consider
`--min-instances 1` for the AI service if cold starts (model load ≈ 10–30 s)
are unacceptable for the demo.

## PDPA & security controls

- **The biometric engine is not internet-reachable**: `flowguard-ai` refuses
  unauthenticated requests at the IAM layer; only the Node backend's service
  account holds `roles/run.invoker`. The app-level `AI_SERVICE_KEY` check
  remains as a second, independent layer.
- **All AI access is RBAC-gated first**: facial recognition/tracking and the
  YOLO proxy (`/api/yolo/*`) require a valid FlowGuard JWT with the same
  FM/Staff roles as the detection dashboards, before any frame is forwarded.
- **No service-account key files** anywhere — identity comes from the attached
  Cloud Run service account via the metadata server.
- **Biometric data never enters an image**: `.dockerignore` files exclude
  `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, screenshots, recordings, databases,
  logs, model caches, `node_modules`, `.venv`, tests, and `.git`.
- **Secrets** live in Secret Manager only — never in Dockerfiles, build args,
  or `VITE_` variables (every `VITE_` value ships to the browser).
- The AI service returns **user IDs, not names**, to callers; names appear in
  developer logs only. Embeddings stay in PostgreSQL; the recognize path never
  persists frames.
- **PDPA retention**: the backend's 90-day transcript cleanup cron starts with
  the server process.
- **Raspberry Pi**: production builds contain **no default Pi address at all**
  (the `raspberrypi.local` fallback is dev-only; kiosk builds opt in via
  `VITE_PI_CAMERA_*`). Without it, scanner pages automatically use the browser
  webcam. The SecurePi edge node pushes alerts *outbound* to
  `/api/edge/detection-alerts` with `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN` — the cloud never
  needs to reach into the LAN.
- Nginx adds `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a referrer
  policy; body size is capped at 50 MB to match the backend.

## Local smoke test

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 --env-file server/.env  <server-image>
docker run --rm -p 8081:8081 -e PORT=8081 --env-file ai-service/.env <ai-image>
docker run --rm -p 8082:8082 -e PORT=8082 -e BACKEND_HOST=<server-host> <client-image>
```

Locally the Node backend sends only `X-AI-Service-Key` (no metadata server
exists off-GCP); on Cloud Run it detects `K_SERVICE` and adds the ID token
automatically. Set `AI_ID_TOKEN=off` to suppress tokens even on Cloud Run
(e.g. if the AI service were ever made public again).

```bash
  --concurrency 8 --timeout 300 \
  --no-allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,NODE_SERVER_URL=$SERVER_URL,USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false,FACE_CTX_ID=-1 \
  --set-secrets DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest
# note the URL -> AI_URL

# 2b) REQUIRED: only the Node backend's service account may invoke the AI service.
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding flowguard-ai --region $REGION \
  --member serviceAccount:$SERVER_SA \
  --role roles/run.invoker

  --image $REG/flowguard-client:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 512Mi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars BACKEND_HOST=${SERVER_URL#https://}
# note the URL -> CLIENT_URL
```

| Service            | Memory | CPU | Concurrency | Notes |
|--------------------|--------|-----|-------------|-------|
| `flowguard-client` | 512 Mi | 1   | default (80)| Nginx + static files; 256 Mi also works |

AI image size ≈ **4.4 GB** (CPU torch, torchvision, 2× OpenCV wheels,
onnxruntime, buffalo_l pack ≈ 280 MB, yolov8n.pt 6.5 MB). Consider
`--min-instances 1` for the AI service if cold starts (model load ≈ 10–30 s)
are unacceptable for the demo.

## PDPA & security controls

- **The biometric engine is not internet-reachable**: `flowguard-ai` refuses
  unauthenticated requests at the IAM layer; only the Node backend's service
  account holds `roles/run.invoker`. The app-level `AI_SERVICE_KEY` check
  remains as a second, independent layer.
- **All AI access is RBAC-gated first**: facial recognition/tracking and the
  YOLO proxy (`/api/yolo/*`) require a valid FlowGuard JWT with the same
  FM/Staff roles as the detection dashboards, before any frame is forwarded.
- **No service-account key files** anywhere — identity comes from the attached
  Cloud Run service account via the metadata server.
- **Biometric data never enters an image**: `.dockerignore` files exclude
  `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, screenshots, recordings, databases,
  logs, model caches, `node_modules`, `.venv`, tests, and `.git`.
- **Secrets** live in Secret Manager only — never in Dockerfiles, build args,
  or `VITE_` variables (every `VITE_` value ships to the browser).
- The AI service returns **user IDs, not names**, to callers; names appear in
  developer logs only. Embeddings stay in PostgreSQL; the recognize path never
  persists frames.
- **PDPA retention**: the backend's 90-day transcript cleanup cron starts with
  the server process.

  (the `raspberrypi.local` fallback is dev-only; kiosk builds opt in via
  `VITE_PI_CAMERA_*`). Without it, scanner pages automatically use the browser
  webcam. The SecurePi edge node pushes alerts *outbound* to
  `/api/edge/detection-alerts` with `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN` — the cloud never
  needs to reach into the LAN.
- Nginx adds `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a referrer
  policy; body size is capped at 50 MB to match the backend.

# FlowGuard — Google Cloud Run deployment (asia-southeast1)

Project: `flowguard-502613`
Artifact Registry: `asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers`

Three services, deployed in this order (each later service needs the earlier one's URL):

| Service            | Source        | Image name          | What it runs                          |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `flowguard-server` | `server/`     | `flowguard-server`  | Node.js/Express API (`node index.js`) |
| `flowguard-ai`     | `ai-service/` | `flowguard-ai`      | FastAPI + InsightFace + YOLOv8 (uvicorn) |
| `flowguard-client` | `client/`     | `flowguard-client`  | React static build behind Nginx reverse proxy |

## Architecture

Same-origin reverse proxy — the browser only ever talks to the frontend origin:

```
Browser ──► flowguard-client (Nginx)
              ├── /api/*, /user/*  ──► flowguard-server (Node)
              ├── /ai/*  (prefix stripped) ──► flowguard-ai (FastAPI YOLO endpoints)
              └── everything else ──► React SPA (index.html fallback for React Router)

flowguard-server ──► flowguard-ai   (face endpoints, X-AI-Service-Key)
flowguard-ai     ──► flowguard-server (detection alerts, x-service-key)
Both            ──► PostgreSQL (external: Neon/Supabase/Cloud SQL)
```

Why this architecture (instead of a build-time `VITE_API_BASE_URL`):

- The Object Detection pages call `/ai/api/yolo/*` as **hardcoded relative
  paths** that previously only worked through the Vite dev proxy. The Nginx
  proxy reproduces that mapping in production with **zero frontend code changes**.
- No backend URL, key, or secret is baked into the image or JS bundle; the
  backend hosts are injected at container start (`BACKEND_HOST`, `AI_HOST`).
- No CORS surface: the browser sees a single origin. Backend CORS
  (`CLIENT_URL`) and AI CORS (`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) remain as defence in depth.
- `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is deliberately left **empty** at build time.

## Cloud Run compliance checklist (already handled in code/images)

- **PORT**: Node resolves `PORT → APP_PORT → 5001` (`server/config/serverConfig.js`);
  the AI image starts `uvicorn --port ${PORT:-8080}`; Nginx listens on `${PORT}`
  via the official image's envsubst templates. **Never set PORT manually** on a
  Cloud Run service — it is injected.
- **0.0.0.0** binding on all three services.
- **No nodemon in production** — the server image installs `--omit=dev` and runs
  `node index.js` (also available as `npm start`).
- **SPA fallback** — Nginx `try_files ... /index.html` for React Router deep links.
- **No localhost between services** — `FACE_AI_URL`, `NODE_SERVER_URL`,
  `PYTHON_AI_URL`, `BACKEND_HOST`, `AI_HOST` all come from env vars.
- **Models baked at build time** — buffalo_l (InsightFace) and yolov8n.pt are
  inside the AI image; nothing downloads at cold start or per request.

## Build & push (run from the repo root — DO NOT run until you intend to deploy)

```bash
gcloud auth configure-docker asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev

REG=asia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/flowguard-502613/flowguard-containers

docker build -t $REG/flowguard-server:v1 server/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 ai-service/
docker build -t $REG/flowguard-client:v1 \
  --build-arg VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=<public-site-key> client/

docker push $REG/flowguard-server:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-ai:v1
docker push $REG/flowguard-client:v1
```

(Or `gcloud builds submit` per directory with the same tags.)

## Deploy

Put every secret in **Secret Manager** first (`APP_SECRET`, `DB_PWD`,
`AI_SERVICE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `SMTP_PASS`, `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN`, …)
and grant the runtime service account `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`.
See [env.example](env.example) for the full variable list per service.

```bash
REGION=asia-southeast1

# 1) Backend
gcloud run deploy flowguard-server \
  --image $REG/flowguard-server:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 1Gi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,DB_SYNC_ALTER=false \
  --set-secrets APP_SECRET=APP_SECRET:latest,DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest,RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:latest,SMTP_PASS=SMTP_PASS:latest,EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN=EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN:latest
# note the URL it prints -> SERVER_URL

# 2) AI service (URL of the backend now exists)
gcloud run deploy flowguard-ai \
  --image $REG/flowguard-ai:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 4Gi --cpu 2 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 \
  --concurrency 8 --timeout 300 --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars DB_HOST=...,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=...,DB_USER=...,NODE_SERVER_URL=$SERVER_URL,USE_SERVER_CAMERA=false,FACE_CTX_ID=-1 \
  --set-secrets DB_PWD=DB_PWD:latest,AI_SERVICE_KEY=AI_SERVICE_KEY:latest
# note the URL -> AI_URL

# 3) Frontend (hostnames only, no https://)
gcloud run deploy flowguard-client \
  --image $REG/flowguard-client:v1 --region $REGION \
  --memory 512Mi --cpu 1 --min-instances 0 --max-instances 3 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars BACKEND_HOST=${SERVER_URL#https://},AI_HOST=${AI_URL#https://}
# note the URL -> CLIENT_URL

# 4) Point the backend's CORS + links at the real frontend URL
gcloud run services update flowguard-server --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars CLIENT_URL=$CLIENT_URL,FRONTEND_URL=$CLIENT_URL

# 5) Tell the AI service which browser origin is allowed (defence in depth)
gcloud run services update flowguard-ai --region $REGION \
  --update-env-vars ALLOWED_ORIGINS=$CLIENT_URL
```

## Recommended resources

| Service            | Memory | CPU | Concurrency | Notes |
|--------------------|--------|-----|-------------|-------|
| `flowguard-client` | 512 Mi | 1   | default (80)| Nginx + static files; 256 Mi also works |
| `flowguard-server` | 1 Gi   | 1   | default (80)| Sequelize sync on boot; 50 MB JSON bodies |
| `flowguard-ai`     | **4 Gi** | **2** | **8**   | buffalo_l (det+recog ONNX) + YOLOv8n resident ≈ 1.5–2.5 GB RSS; per-request numpy/cv2 spikes. 2 vCPU keeps analyze-frame latency usable on CPU. Set `--timeout 300`. |

AI image size estimate: **≈ 2.5–3.5 GB** (CPU torch ≈ 900 MB, torchvision,
2× OpenCV wheels, onnxruntime, buffalo_l pack ≈ 280 MB, yolov8n.pt 6.5 MB).
Consider `--min-instances 1` for the AI service if cold starts (model load
≈ 10–30 s) are unacceptable for the demo.

## PDPA & security controls

- **Biometric data never enters an image**: `.dockerignore` files exclude
  `.env*`, face images, `known_faces/`, screenshots, recordings, databases,
  logs, model caches, `node_modules`, `.venv`, tests, and `.git`.
- **Secrets** live in Secret Manager only — never in Dockerfiles, build args,
  or `VITE_` variables (every `VITE_` value ships to the browser).
- **Face endpoints** (`/api/encode-faces`, `/user/recognize`, `/user/track`,
  `/refresh`) require `AI_SERVICE_KEY` — set it on BOTH services or the AI
  service runs unprotected (it prints a warning in dev mode).
- The AI service returns **user IDs, not names**, to callers; names appear in
  developer logs only. Embeddings stay in PostgreSQL; the recognize path never
  persists frames.
- **PDPA retention**: the backend's 90-day transcript cleanup cron starts with
  the server process.
- **Raspberry Pi**: no private Pi IP is baked into the public bundle (the
  fallback is the mDNS name `raspberrypi.local`; real Pi URLs come from
  `VITE_PI_CAMERA_*` env at build for kiosk builds only). The SecurePi edge
  node pushes alerts *outbound* to `/api/edge/detection-alerts` with
  `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN` — the cloud never needs to reach into the LAN.
- Nginx adds `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a referrer
  policy; body size is capped at 50 MB to match the backend.

## Local smoke test

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 --env-file server/.env  <server-image>
docker run --rm -p 8081:8081 -e PORT=8081 --env-file ai-service/.env <ai-image>
docker run --rm -p 8082:8082 -e PORT=8082 \
  -e BACKEND_HOST=<server-host> -e AI_HOST=<ai-host> <client-image>
```

# FlowGuard — Cloud Run environment variables (asia-southeast1, project flowguard-502613)
# Placeholders only — NEVER commit real values. Store secrets in Secret Manager
# and reference them from the Cloud Run service (--set-secrets), not --set-env-vars.
#
# IMPORTANT: never set PORT on any service — Cloud Run injects it automatically
# and rejects services that try to set it manually.

# =============================================================================
# 1. flowguard-server  (Node.js backend, server/Dockerfile)
# =============================================================================

# --- Secrets (Secret Manager) ---
APP_SECRET=your-jwt-signing-secret
DB_PWD=your-db-password
AI_SERVICE_KEY=your-shared-ai-service-secret          # must equal the AI service's AI_SERVICE_KEY
RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=your-recaptcha-secret-key
SMTP_PASS=your-google-app-password
EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN=your-securepi-ingest-token          # SecurePi -> /api/edge/detection-alerts
EDGE_SERVICE_TOKEN=your-edge-device-token             # optional; unset disables the edge-token path
WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-whatsapp-access-token      # only if WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true

# --- Plain env vars ---
# CORS + link generation: the deployed FRONTEND Cloud Run URL.
CLIENT_URL=https://flowguard-client-xxxxxxxxxx.asia-southeast1.run.app
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=
FRONTEND_URL=https://flowguard-client-xxxxxxxxxx.asia-southeast1.run.app

# PostgreSQL (Neon/Supabase/Cloud SQL — must be reachable from Cloud Run).
DB_HOST=your-db-host
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=your-db-name
DB_USER=your-db-user

# FastAPI AI service BASE url (Cloud Run URL of flowguard-ai) — paths are appended.
# NEVER localhost in the cloud.
FACE_AI_URL=https://flowguard-ai-xxxxxxxxxx.asia-southeast1.run.app
# Teammate-owned incident-scan FULL endpoint url (includes /recognize).
# Leave unset if that separate service is not deployed — the route returns 503 cleanly.
PYTHON_AI_URL=

# Schema alteration is opt-in; leave false for normal deploys.
DB_SYNC_ALTER=false

# SMTP (password reset emails)
SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_SECURE=false
SMTP_USER=flowguard-example@gmail.com
MAIL_FROM="FlowGuard <flowguard-example@gmail.com>"

# WhatsApp driver notifications — keep false unless real credentials exist.
WHATSAPP_ENABLED=false
WHATSAPP_API_URL=https://graph.facebook.com/v20.0
WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=your-meta-phone-number-id

# =============================================================================
# 2. flowguard-ai  (Python FastAPI AI service, ai-service/Dockerfile)
# =============================================================================

# --- Secrets (Secret Manager) ---
#DB_PWD=your-db-password                              # same database as the backend
#AI_SERVICE_KEY=your-shared-ai-service-secret         # MUST match the backend's value

# --- Plain env vars ---
#DB_HOST=your-db-host
#DB_PORT=5432
#DB_NAME=your-db-name
#DB_USER=your-db-user

# Node backend BASE url — used to POST detection alerts. NEVER localhost in the cloud.
NODE_SERVER_URL=https://flowguard-server-xxxxxxxxxx.asia-southeast1.run.app

# Browser origins allowed by CORS for the YOLO endpoints. With the Nginx

# FlowGuard React frontend — Cloud Run image (static build served by Nginx).
#
# Architecture: same-origin reverse proxy. The production bundle is built with
# VITE_API_BASE_URL left EMPTY, so every API call stays a relative URL
# (/api, /user, /ai) and Nginx forwards it to the Node/AI Cloud Run services
# at runtime (see nginx.conf). Benefits:
#   - no backend URL or secret is baked into the image or JS bundle;
#   - no CORS exposure (browser only sees one origin);
#   - the hardcoded /ai/* YOLO paths keep working exactly as they do behind
#     the Vite dev proxy.
#
# Do NOT pass secrets as build args — every VITE_ value ships to the browser.
# The only build-time value a deployment may optionally supply is the PUBLIC
# reCAPTCHA site key.

FROM node:22-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
# Public (browser-visible) value only. Never pass secrets here.
ARG VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=""
ENV VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=${VITE_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY}
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:1.27-alpine
# The nginx entrypoint runs envsubst on *.template files at startup, injecting
# PORT (from Cloud Run) plus BACKEND_HOST / AI_HOST (service env vars).
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
# Default for local `docker run`; Cloud Run always overrides PORT itself.
ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080

content.text:
Rearchitecture complete and fully validated. Here's the report:

## 1. Architecture change

The AI service is now **private**: `Browser → Nginx (client) → Node backend → private Python AI service`. The client Nginx proxies **only** `/api/*` and `/user/*` to the Node backend — the `/ai/*` passthrough is gone from both [nginx.conf](client/nginx.conf) and the Vite dev proxy ([vite.config.js](client/vite.config.js)), so dev and prod have identical topology. The browser never reaches FastAPI in any environment.

## 2. Routes changed

- **New Node proxy** [server/routes/yolo.js](server/routes/yolo.js), mounted at `/api/yolo` in [index.js](server/index.js): `GET /api/yolo/people-count` and `POST /api/yolo/analyze-frame`, both gated by `verifyToken + requireRole('FM','Staff')` (same RBAC as the detection dashboards). The analyze-frame proxy validates the data-URL image, caps it at 8 MB, and forwards **only** whitelisted fields (`image`, `camera_id`, `zone_id`, `source`).
- **Facial tracking/recognition/enrolment** were already Node-proxied (`/api/facial-recognition/*`, `/user/enroll-face`) — reused, now upgraded with ID-token auth.
- **Client**: [ObjectDetection.jsx](client/src/pages/ObjectDetection.jsx) and [CameraFeed.jsx](client/src/pages/CameraFeed.jsx) now call `/api/yolo/*` with the JWT `Authorization` header instead of `/ai/api/yolo/*` unauthenticated.

## 3. Private AI authentication

New [server/services/aiServiceAuth.js](server/services/aiServiceAuth.js): `aiServiceHeaders(targetUrl)` fetches a Google-signed ID token from the **Cloud Run metadata server** using the service's **attached service account** (no JSON key files anywhere), with the audience set to the AI service's URL origin (works for both `FACE_AI_URL` and the path-bearing `PYTHON_AI_URL`). Tokens are cached per-audience and refreshed 60 s before expiry. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` alongside the retained `X-AI-Service-Key` (defence in depth — FastAPI still validates it itself). All six Node→AI call sites now use it: the YOLO proxy, both recognize calls and track in [facialRecognition.js](server/routes/facialRecognition.js), encode-faces and both `/refresh` calls in [user.js](server/routes/user.js), and the incident scan in [incident.js](server/routes/incident.js). The README documents deploying the AI service with `--no-allow-unauthenticated` and granting the Node service account `roles/run.invoker` on it.

## 4. Local-development fallback

Token fetching activates only when `K_SERVICE` is present (set by Cloud Run itself) or `AI_ID_TOKEN=force`; `AI_ID_TOKEN=off` disables it. Locally the metadata server is never contacted and headers contain just `X-AI-Service-Key` — `npm run dev` needs no Google credentials. This is covered by tests.

## 5. Pi URL behaviour

[piCamera.js](client/src/constants/piCamera.js): the `raspberrypi.local` fallback is now **dev-only** (`import.meta.env.DEV`). Production/cloud builds ship **no default Pi address** — verified by grepping the built bundle (zero matches for `raspberrypi.local`, private IPs, `/ai/api`, or localhost). With no Pi URL configured, `isPiCameraReachable()` returns false immediately, so every scanner page falls back to the browser webcam; uploaded-video mode and the authenticated SecurePi edge-ingestion route (`/api/edge/detection-alerts`, outbound-push with `EDGE_INGEST_TOKEN`) are untouched.

## 6. Files changed

**New:** `server/routes/yolo.js`, `server/services/aiServiceAuth.js`, `server/tests/.../yoloProxy.test.js` (13 tests). **Modified:** `server/index.js`, `server/routes/facialRecognition.js`, `server/routes/user.js`, `server/routes/incident.js`, `client/nginx.conf`, `client/Dockerfile` (comment), `client/vite.config.js`, `client/src/pages/ObjectDetection.jsx`, `client/src/pages/CameraFeed.jsx` + its test, `client/tests/.../ObjectDetectionSourceModes.test.jsx`, `client/src/constants/piCamera.js`, `deployment/cloud-run/README.md`, `deployment/cloud-run/env.example`. Env changes: client no longer needs `AI_HOST`; server gains optional `AI_ID_TOKEN` override.

## 7. Test & build results — all passing

- **Client Vitest: 433/433** (47 files). One file (ApiBase.test.jsx, unrelated to these changes) timed out once while a Docker build was saturating the CPU; it passes in isolation and the full suite passed cleanly on the quiet rerun.
- **Client production build:** OK; bundle verified free of Pi/AI/localhost addresses.
- **Server Jest: 402/402** (29 suites — up from 389/28 with the new proxy+auth suite).
- **Python pytest: 8/8.**
- **Docker builds:** all three images rebuilt successfully (server 375 MB, client 142 MB, AI 4.37 GB).
- **Smoke tests:** client container serves the SPA with React Router deep-link fallback on the injected PORT, and `/ai/...` now returns the SPA (text/html) instead of proxying; AI container boots uvicorn on the injected PORT with models loaded from the baked-in cache (no downloads); server container binds `0.0.0.0:$PORT` and serves `/` even with the DB unreachable.

## 8. Git state

Nothing committed, pushed, staged, or reset — HEAD remains `f28a005` on `deploy/staging`, all changes are unstaged working-tree modifications and untracked files. No cloud resources were created or modified.
